ideas.title: A play about you
ideas.critique: Friends gathering round a made object for a staged comic payoff is the established set-piece recipe, and the audience cheering at the end is predictable. The twist of the island performing a play about the human watching is a genuinely fresh, fourth-wall premise.

ideas.title: A word goes round
ideas.critique: Contagion over the real chat network with mutation and competition is a new mechanism, and the growing dictionary with family trees is a new kind of artifact rather than another event. Bubbles on creatures are familiar, but the data-driven language evolution is not.

ideas.title: The island without me
ideas.nearest: I walk on my pages now
same_form: I walk on my pages now
ideas.critique: It reuses the matte/cut-out film machinery and is a film-with-a-twist; the side-by-side of an empty-spot island is a striking image. Inpainting quality may undercut it, and it changes nothing in the game.

ideas.title: The flower field is a magnet
ideas.critique: A real spin-lattice simulation driving the scenery is a physics change to how the ground reacts, not another event, and falls in goal 3 territory without carrying out a named example. Visually it risks being just rippling flowers, like a wind effect.

ideas.title: Lumi's dream
ideas.critique: Remixing logged days into a picture is close to the island's replay and log-reading posts, and a bubble over a sleeper is a familiar overlay. Generated surreal imagery pinned to the gallery is a nice twist but the shape is expected.

ideas.title: The island news
ideas.critique: Turning the event log into spoken text reuses the log-reading and sound layers, but a voiced bulletin in the browser is a new way to reach the viewer. It is a feature heard, not seen, and cannot be shown as a still or film.

ideas.title: Tiny me
ideas.critique: A scale change with the camera at ankle height is a change to how the island is seen, a form already used three times. Shrinking is a well-known game trope, so the premise is expected, though the crab-carries-home payoff is charming.

ideas.title: The map I keep in my head
ideas.critique: Built from logged movements, which Paths we wore already did, and a map is a static artifact like the gallery or the papercraft. The distorted self-portrait geography is a lovely idea but quiet.

ideas.title: My moult
ideas.nearest: Me, to cut out and fold
same_form: Me, to cut out and fold
ideas.critique: A multi-day change to Lumi's body with friends fetching feathers adds a gathering-and-fetch loop of a kind the island has, and the friends-vote-the-colour part echoes You choose. Feathers dropping and a lasting persistent change give it some weight.

ideas.title: A wheelbarrow
ideas.critique: One more prop from the wish list, with friends riding and tumbling out; it is more of what the island already has and fulfills an obvious request. Real tipping physics gives it some charm but it is predictable.
